survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive results for Serbia using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The note does not specify whether student/sampling weights or replicate weights were applied in the production of the displayed estimates, nor does it name any weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate design (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Because the factsheet is a secondary reporting product rather than an author-led microdata ML analysis, the weighting and variance estimation procedures are handled within the OECD/PISA production pipeline and are not documented here. For analysts reproducing these estimates from microdata, complex survey weights and PISA replicate methods should be used to obtain correct standard errors and confidence intervals for means and proportions.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a PISA 2022 results factsheet that reports proficiency-level shares and mean performance summaries rather than providing an analysis pipeline with PV generation/combining or missing-data imputation details. Plausible Values are part of the underlying PISA scaling for cognitive achievement, but the factsheet does not describe PV handling because it is not conducting a new student-level empirical model in the text provided. Missing-data handling is therefore not reported at the level of methodological choices (e.g., deletion vs imputation) in this factsheet.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports the Serbia analytic sample as 6,413 students in 183 schools who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, representing about 59,300 15-year-olds (an estimated 87% of the total population of 15-year-olds). No additional inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., missing-data exclusions, grade restrictions beyond the 15-year-old target, or specific subject-only subsamples) are described beyond the stated completion of the assessment in one of the three domains.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Serbia performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how performance relates to equity and school experiences. It reports mean performance trends (2012–2022), proficiency-level distributions (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6 shares), and gaps by socio-economic status (ESCS quintiles/quartiles), gender, and immigrant background, alongside contextual indicators such as belonging, discipline, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning disruptions. The note also describes the PISA 2022 assessment structure: two two-hour subject tests with different item sets across students, a background questionnaire for students, and a principal questionnaire. It further states that Serbia met PISA technical quality standards for reporting in 2022. Because this is a descriptive factsheet rather than an author-led predictive modeling study, no ML model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/R²) are provided.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (a descriptive reporting product) rather than an empirical ML paper. As a result, there is no author-specified predictive modeling design, no ML algorithms, no PV-combining or missing-data strategy described in the text, and no target-variable-specific model metrics to populate main_findings. The sparse methodological fields are therefore consistent with the document’s purpose: communicating PISA results and contextual patterns for Serbia using OECD’s established assessment and scaling procedures.
